title: Purview treats ChatGPT Enterprise and Claude Enterprise as first-class enterprise AI apps
summary: Microsoft Purview's generative AI documentation groups supported apps into Copilot experiences, Enterprise AI apps, and Other AI apps. The Enterprise AI apps category explicitly includes Entra-registered AI apps, Microsoft Foundry, ChatGPT Enterprise and Anthropic Claude (Enterprise), while browser-detected Generative AI (ChatGPT consumer, Google Gemini, consumer Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek and peers) lands under Other AI apps in Defender for Cloud Apps. DSPM / DSPM for AI remains the recommended front door for discovery, oversharing insights and one-click policy recommendations.
why: If your AI programme only hardens Microsoft Copilot, Purview is already telling you the rest of the estate is visible — and differently controlled. Use the Enterprise AI vs Other AI split to drive approved inventory, SSO and Endpoint DLP rather than a single 'block all AI' reflex.
todo: Open DSPM / DSPM for AI and review which Enterprise AI apps versus Other AI apps appear for your tenant.
Align the approved-tools inventory with Purview's categories: Enterprise SKUs behind SSO; consumer Generative AI as Denied for company data.
Pair Endpoint DLP and Cloud App controls for unsanctioned browser AI with Conditional Access on Entra-registered enterprise AI apps.
Read the enterprise AI governance pillar for the multi-vendor control plane that sits above Copilot-only rollout work.
effective_note: Capability documentation on Microsoft Learn (Purview AI protections page), checked 2026-11-06. Not a new product launch announcement.
